packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-19 - unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet. Nothing done beyond the brief's rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (face 1, overview image-001.jpg)
- Two small detached paper fragments on black ground, with colour checker and cm scale. Both carry modern pencil shelfmark notes ("Stams, STA Frag. 181-1r" on the upper piece; "Stams, STA, Frag. 181-2r" on the lower piece). A grey redaction box covers part of the lower piece.
- Upper fragment (~8 x 5 cm): text in a cursive/humanistic-looking hand, ink brown. On the left is a narrow strip of text in a smaller, fainter hand (looks like the end of a neighbouring column or marginal note, partly cut), separated from the main block. Main block: ~7 visible lines, cut off at right and bottom. One line (line 3) appears underlined ("est. quia non amant, non desid-"). A line begins "Aug. de ..." (citation marker, observation only).
- Lower fragment (~12 x 4 cm): a strip with one partly cut top line (only lower parts of letters), then 2 full lines in the same kind of hand, then a short catchword/note at right ("gra"?) and lower area mostly blank/redacted. Left and right edges cut.
- No rubrics, enlarged initials or colour visible at overview scale.
- Orientation: upright.

TILE image-002.jpg (native; left half of upper fragment, Frag. 181-1r)
Shows the left-hand note block (4 lines, smaller hand, fainter) and the left ends of 7 main-text lines. The note block's last word in line 2 runs right up into the main-text "Quando", so the note block looks like a marginal addition squeezed in beside the main text (interpretation). Below the note block: modern pencil "Stams, STA / Frag. 181-1r".

Left note block (marginal?):
002-L1  gra(tia)~ n(on)? desideriu(m)? req(ui)rit
002-L2  sicut ignis ligni(s)? sic gra(tia)
002-L3  alacritate et desiderio
002-L4  indiget Chrysost(omus)   [read "Chrysost" with a final abbreviated -t; "Chry" a little uncertain]
 notes: L1 "n" with a mark - could be n(on) or n(ostra)?; "desideriu" ends with a stroke; "reqrit" with mark over q = req(ui)rit?. L2 "ligni(s)?" - final letter uncertain (ligni / lignis / ligna?).

Main text, left portions (lines continue onto image-003):
002-M1  Unde illud E[...]   [first word "Vnde" / "Unde"; small cramped - maybe "Unde" with superscript; reading tentative]
002-M2  Quando q(ue)? res [...]   ["g" with a superscript mark = q(ue)? or q(uando)?; enlarged initial-style Q in plain ink]
002-M3  est. quia non [...]   (underlined)
002-M4  Aug. de [struck-through word, "ug..." / "ingr..."] [...]
002-M5  ge grauissimu(m)? [...]   [first word "ge" = (er)ge? / (re)ge?; uncertain]
002-M6  e(st)? alia grau[...]   [first sign looks like a "9"/"e" with stroke; then "alia"; next word begins "grau" / "gran"]
002-M7  tyrannus; a[...]   [a horizontal stroke over/through the "t" - looks like a cross-bar]
002-M8  [tops of letters only, cut at bottom edge]

TILE image-003.jpg (native; right half of upper fragment, overlapping image-002 by ~1-2 words). Right edge of fragment cuts every line.
Combined main-text lines (002 left + 003 right; overlap words counted once):
003-M1  Unde illud Ezechielis. Sicut p[...]   ["Ezechielis" fairly clear; "Unde" first word still tentative; last letter cut]
003-M2  Quando g° (= ergo?) res sic se habet, quid ca[...]   [sign is a g-shape with small o above; I take it as ergo, tentative]
003-M3  est. quia non amant, non deside[...]   (whole line underlined by a ruled stroke)
003-M4  Aug. de [word struck through: "ing"/"ug"?] p(re)ceptis? leue est a[...]   [p with a superscript mark (looks like a small c/hook) then "ceptis" or "ceptid"; "leue" clear]
003-M5  [er]ge? grauissimum, amor [n with stroke / "in"?] dulcora[t?][...]   [before "dulcora" a loop-like mark, perhaps a correction or "n."; "dulcora" clear]
003-M6  e(st)? alia grauis? re sitienti; ci[...]   ["grauis"/"quauis" uncertain; "sitienti" clear]
003-M7  tyrannus; appetenti iusculu(m)?   [last word: "iusculu" or "insculu"; final stroke cut by edge]
003-M8  [tops of letters only]

TILE image-004.jpg (native; left part of lower fragment, Frag. 181-2r). Left edge cuts line starts. Top line trimmed through the letters (only lower two-thirds visible).
004-L1  [...]ygam? aliq(ua)m? quid e(st)? dulce ho(m)i(n)b(us)?; sper[...] / super in[...]   [line cut through by top edge; "dulce" fairly sure; "hoibg" = ho(m)i(n)b(us)? with -us sign; "sper"/"super" with stroke through p]
004-L2  [...]ona, s(ed) gr(ati)a adiuuare ut sint ho(m)i(ni) facilia et [...]   [first word ends "-ona" (bona?); "s3" = s(ed); "gra" with overline = gr(ati)a; "hoi" with overline = homini]
004-L3  [...]a, nec terra sine pluuia fert fructu(s)?, sic nec gr(ati)a[...]   ["fructg" with -us sign]
004-L4  [a short stroke, then faint letters partly hidden by the grey redaction box; illegible traces]
Below: modern pencil "Stams, S[TA ...]" (continues on image-005).

TILE image-005.jpg (native; right part of lower fragment, overlaps image-004 by ~2-3 words). Right edge torn but text appears to end within the leaf on lines 2-3 (possible line ends, not certain).
Combined lower-fragment lines:
005-L1  [...]ygam? aliq(ua)m? quid e(st)? dulce ho(m)i(n)b(us)?; s(em)per? inat? .   [after "hoibg;" a "sper" with stroke through descender (s(em)per or s(u)per?) then "inat" with a superscript mark (innat? / in(n)at?) and a point; line top cut]
005-L2  [...]ona, s(ed) gr(ati)a adiuuare ut sint ho(m)i(ni) facilia et meritoria simul. Sicut n(on)? pluuia   [after "Sicut" a single "n" with a point/mark: n(on)? or "n."?; "meritoria" first letter partly lost in a pale abrasion]
005-L3  [...]a, nec terra sine pluuia fert fructu(s), sic nec gr(ati)a sine uoluntate nec uoluntas sine
005-L4  (turned down at right, below L3:)  gr(ati)a .   [gra with overline, written under the end of L3 as a turn-down]
Below: grey redaction box; modern pencil "Stams, STA, Frag. 181-2r".

LAYOUT SURVEY (face 2, overview image-006.jpg)
- Versos of the same two fragments: upper "Stams, STA, Frag. 181-1v" (most of the upper area covered by a grey redaction box; visible paper below appears blank); lower "Stams, STA, Frag. 181-2v": appears essentially blank, with a few faint ink marks near the top centre (possibly show-through or a stray stroke). Reading tiles 007-010 to check.

TILES image-007.jpg and image-008.jpg (native; left and right halves of upper fragment verso, Frag. 181-1v)
- Grey redaction box covers the upper ~45% of the fragment. Visible paper below the box shows no medieval/early-modern text, only foxing specks and the modern pencil "Stams, STA, Frag. 181-1v". No writing readable; whatever lies under the box is not available.

TILES image-009.jpg and image-010.jpg (native; left and right parts of lower fragment verso, Frag. 181-2v)
- No text block. Near the top edge on image-010 (~line 1 position) there are faint ink traces: a short form like "ma" / "ina" with a dark dot and stroke at left and a short oblique stroke further right. These are at the very top edge and likely the cut-off descenders/feet of a line, or show-through; not readable as words. Otherwise blank paper with foxing; modern pencil "Stams, STA, Frag. 181-2v".

SUMMARY OF READING / LIMITATIONS
- Readable text is on the rectos only (181-1r upper strip, 181-2r lower strip); versos blank except a redaction box on 181-1v and stray traces on 181-2v.
- Paper, cursive early-modern-looking hand (observation of script only; no dating claimed). Latin. Frequent abbreviations: gr(ati)a with overline, s3 = s(ed), ho(m)i(ni) with overline, -us sign (g-shape) in hoibg / fructg, g with superscript o (read as ergo, tentative).
- Upper strip: 7 main lines + a 4-line note block at left in a smaller hand (main text vs note is an interpretation). Main lines cut at right; bottom line only tops of letters. One line underlined. One word struck through in line 4.
- Lower strip: 3 lines + a turn-down "gra(tia)"; top line cut through the letters; left edge cuts line starts; right end of lines 2-3 probably near the true line end.
- Whether the two strips are from the same leaf/sequence is not determinable from the images; I have not ordered them textually.
- Selected spans: all visible text on both rectos was transcribed; nothing left unread except the redacted areas and the cut tops/bottoms.
- Main uncertainties: 002/003-M1 first word; M2 "g°"; M4 struck word and "p(re)ceptis"; M5 first word and the mark before "dulcora"; M6 "grauis"; M7 "iusculu"; lower L1 "ygam? aliqm" and "sper inat"; L2 "n" after Sicut; marginal L1 "n desideriu reqrit".
- Did not hit the image limit.
